description:
Blazing-fast Claude in your terminal — a C++26 alternative to claude-code.

agentty is a native C++26 terminal coding agent and a drop-in alternative to claude-code. A single static binary with sub-millisecond cold start, sandboxed by default, and one-command SSH air-gap. No Node, Python, or Electron. Signs in with your Claude Pro/Max subscription or an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
Added
- Hooks speak Claude Code's protocol, so RTK works as is (#128). A
  hooks.json can use Claude Code's shape (PreToolUse, PostToolUse,
  PostToolUseFailure). Hooks get the event as JSON on stdin and can deny,
  ask, allow, rewrite a call before it runs, or replace its output before the
  model reads it. PreToolUse runs before the permission prompt, so the
  prompt and the card show what will really run. Hooks now also run in
  agentty run and in subagents. The old pre_tool / post_tool format
  still works. See Hooks.
- Delete, Home and End work in the prompt, the login box and the settings
  add field (#129). Thanks @sail3r.
- 32-bit programs run in the sandbox on x86_64 Linux with multilib (#130).
  Thanks @lukerb52. They get their own syscall filter, which allows exactly
  what the 64-bit one does by name; claybin's new x86_audit test keeps the
  two equal.
Changed
- The ^U thinking reader ends like the transcript's block: Reasoned · 216 tokens · 4.3s · 50 tok/s, and a long block gets a scrollbar.
- Overlay scrollbars are a block thumb in the panel's colour, with no
  track line beside the border, and move in half-cell steps.
- Stats columns are sized to their content. Text and donuts take what
  they need, charts take the rest, so the gap beside Latency is gone.
Fixed
- Common tools no longer fail inside the sandbox. sqlite said "disk I/O
  error", git with core.fsync died on fsync, and flock, file watchers
  (tsc --watch, vite), Rust panic handlers and node timers all hit
  "Operation not permitted". The sandbox now allows those calls (fsync,
  flock, inotify, sigaltstack, umask and others); each one only acts on what
  the program can already reach. nice works on the program itself.
- The ^U reader no longer cuts lines with … or draws empty rows after the
  text.
- A sandboxed hook can read its input. It used to get a payload file in a
  /tmp the sandbox couldn't see.
